They all agree on the long-vowel reading in His saying: ﴿And what you give in zakāh﴾. The root meaning of ribā is increase. The short-vowel reading returns to the meaning of the long-vowel reading, because its meaning is "what you did in the manner of giving," just as you say: "I came in error" and "I came in rightness." The meaning in the verse is: what you give of excess that is free of any return. ﴿So that it may increase within the wealth of people﴾, meaning: so that it may grow and be purified within their wealth. ﴿It does not increase with Allah﴾, meaning: Allah does not bless it.

As-Suddī said: Ribā in this place is the gift that a man gives to his brother seeking a reward in return, for that does not increase with Allah, meaning its giver is not rewarded for it and there is no sin upon him. Qatādah and aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.

Al-Wāḥidī said: This is the view of the majority of the exegetes (mufassirūn).

Az-Zajjāj said: That is, a person gives something so that he may be repaid with more than it. That is not forbidden, but there is no reward for it, because the one who gives it seeks in return something greater than it.

Ash-Shaʿbī said: The meaning of the verse is that whatever a person serves another with, in order to benefit from him in his worldly life, that benefit which repays the service does not increase with Allah.

It has been said that this was forbidden to the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, based on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And do not confer favor seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:6]. Its meaning is: that you give and then take more than it in return.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning the gift given for reward (hibat al-thawāb).

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: And what is similar to it, of what a person does in order to be repaid for it.

ʿIkrimah said: Ribā is of two kinds: a lawful ribā and a forbidden ribā. As for the lawful ribā, it is the gift that a person gives seeking what is better than it, as in this verse.

It has also been said that what is in this verse is the forbidden ribā. According to this view, the meaning of "it does not increase with Allah" is that Allah does not reckon it as increase, but it belongs to the one from whom it was taken.

Al-Muhallab said: The scholars have differed concerning one who gives a gift seeking a reward. Mālik said: It is to be examined. If the one of its kind is one who seeks a reward from the recipient, then he has that right, like the gift of a poor man to a rich man, the gift of a servant to his master, and the gift of a man to his ruler. This is one of the two opinions of ash-Shāfiʿī. Abū Ḥanīfah said: He has no reward if he did not stipulate it. This is ash-Shāfiʿī's other opinion.

The majority read liyarbuwa with the letter yā' (third person), with the verb attributed to the pronoun referring to ribā. Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read it with tā' (second person) with a vowel on it, addressing the group, meaning: so that you may become people of increases.

Abū Mālik read: "li-tur'ūhā" [liturbūhā]. The meaning of the verse is that it does not grow with Allah, and He does not reward it, because He accepts only what is intended for His Face sincerely for Him alone. ﴿And what you give in zakāh, seeking the Face of Allah﴾, meaning: (p-1136) and what you give in charity without seeking a return by it, aiming only at what is with Allah. ﴿Those are the ones who multiply﴾. The muḍʿif (one who multiplies) is one who is multiplied beyond the manifold increases of good deeds, those who are given ten times its like up to seven hundredfold.

Al-Farrāʾ said: This is like their saying: muslim (one who has fat camels), mu ʿṭish (one who has thirsty camels), and muḍʿif (one who has weak camels), when he has camels that are fat, or thirsty, or weak.

Ubayy read al-muḍʿafūn with a fatḥah on the ʿayn, as a passive participle (ism mafʿūl).

﴿Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that?﴾ He, glorified is He, returned to arguing against the polytheists, and that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Causer of death and the Giver of life. Then He said, in the form of a question: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does any of that?﴾ It is known that they would say: there is none among them who does any of that, so the proof is established against them. Then He, glorified is He, declared Himself transcendent, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate﴾, meaning: they have glorified Him with a true glorification, and He is exalted above being subject to any of that. His saying ﴿of your partners﴾ is a predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam), with min indicating partial (lil-tabʿīḍ). The subject is the relative pronoun: that is, man yaf al (who does). ﴿Of that of yours﴾ is attached to something omitted, because it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of the thing mentioned after it. The min in min shayʾ is extra, for emphasis. He attributed the partners to them because they used to call them gods and assign to them a share of their wealth.

﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned.﴾ Glorified is He, explained that polytheism and sins are the cause of the appearance of corruption in the world.

Interpreters have differed concerning the meaning of the appearance of the corruption mentioned. It has been said: it is drought, the lack of vegetation, the decrease of provision, the prevalence of fear, and similar things. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: The corruption on land is the killing of the son of Adam his brother, meaning the killing of Qābīl of Hābīl. And at sea it is the king who used to seize every ship by force.

I wonder what proof led them to this distant specification and this strange determination, for the verse was revealed to Muḥammad (ﷺ), and the definite form of "corruption" indicates the category, so it includes every corruption occurring in the realms of land and sea.

As-Suddī said: The corruption is polytheism, which is the greatest corruption.

It may be said that although polytheism is the complete example among kinds of sins, there is no proof that it is specifically what is meant.

It has also been said: The corruption is the slump of prices and the scarcity of livelihood. It has been said: The corruption is the cutting of roads and oppression. It has been said: other than that, which is specification without proof.

The apparent meaning of the verse is the appearance of whatever it is correct to call corruption, whether it returns to the actions of the children of Adam, their sins, their committing of evil deeds, their severing of ties, their oppression, and their fighting one another, or returns to what comes from Allah, glorified is He, because of their sins, such as drought, prevalence of fear, death, decrease of crops, and decrease of fruits.

Al-barr (land) and al-baḥr (sea) are the well-known things. It has been said: al-barr is the deserts, and al-baḥr is the towns that are on water, as ʿIkrimah said, and the Arabs call great cities "seas." Mujāhid said: al-barr is what is of cities and villages not on a river, and al-baḥr is what is on the bank of a river. The first view is more preferable.

The meaning of al-barr would be the cities of the land, and the meaning of al-baḥr would be the cities of the sea, and what is connected to the cities of their farms and pastures. The bāʾ in ﴿by what﴾ indicates cause, and mā is either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah). ﴿So that He may make them taste part of what they have done﴾. The lām is connected to ẓahara (appeared), and it is the lām of cause, meaning: so that He may make them taste the punishment of part of their deeds, or the recompense of their deeds. ﴿Perhaps they will return﴾ from what they are engaged in of sins, and repent to Allah.

The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) and to his community, who follow him in this, or to every responsible person who has wealth that Allah has made abundant for him. He gave precedence to kindness toward relatives, because the best charity is that given to a near relative. It is a charity that is multiplied, and it is also the maintaining of ties of kinship (ṣilat al-raḥim), which is recommended. What is meant is kindness toward them through charity, maintaining ties, and righteousness. ﴿And the needy and the wayfarer﴾, meaning: give the needy and the wayfarer their right, which they deserve.

The reason the three categories are singled out for mention is that they have a greater claim to kindness than other categories. Giving them is an obligation upon everyone who has wealth beyond his own sufficiency and the sufficiency of those he supports.

It has also been said that the "near of kin" in the verse means the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: And what is similar to it, of what a person does in order to be repaid for it.

As for the riba that is no harm, it is a man's gift to another man, desiring its excess and multiples.

al-Bayhaqi related from him, who said: "This is the permissible riba: that one gives a gift desiring more than it, and there is neither reward nor sin for it. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade this specifically, saying: ﴿and do not give, seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 6]."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: ﴿And whatever you give in zakah﴾, he said: "It is the charity."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾, he said: "The land is the desert that has no river nearby, and the sea is what is of the cities and villages on the bank of a river."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding the verse, he said: "The decrease of blessing due to the deeds of the servants, so that they may repent."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also: ﴿so that they may return﴾, he said: "from sins."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: ﴿they will be divided﴾, he said: "they will disperse."

When Allah, glorified is He, explained how the command of Allah should be honored, He pointed to what is due in support of kin and those in need, from among those whom Allah has granted abundance in provision. So He said: ﴿So give the near of kin his right﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) and to his community, who follow him in this, or to every responsible person who has wealth that Allah has made abundant for him. He gave precedence to kindness toward relatives, because the best charity is that given to a near relative. It is a charity that is multiplied, and it is also the maintaining of ties of kinship (ṣilat al-raḥim), which is recommended. What is meant is kindness toward them through charity, maintaining ties, and righteousness. ﴿And the needy and the wayfarer﴾, meaning: give the needy and the wayfarer their right, which they deserve.

The reason the three categories are singled out for mention is that they have a greater claim to kindness than other categories. Giving them is an obligation upon everyone who has wealth beyond his own sufficiency and the sufficiency of those he supports.

Scholars have differed over whether this verse is muḥkam (not abrogated, Arabic: muḥkam) or mansūkh (abrogated by a later ruling, naskh). It has been said that it is mansūkh, abrogated by the verses of inheritance. It has also been said that it is muḥkam, and that a relative has a binding right in the wealth of a wealthy relative. This is the view of Mujāhid and Qatādah.

Mujāhid said: No charity is accepted from anyone while his kinsman is in need.

Muqātil said: The right of the needy is that he be given charity, and the right of the wayfarer is hospitality.

It has also been said that the "near of kin" in the verse means the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Qurṭubī said: The first view is more sound, for their right is explained in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near of kin﴾ [al-Anfāl 8:41]. Al-Ḥasan said: The command to give to the near of kin is for recommendation (nadb). ﴿That is best for those who seek the Face of Allah﴾, meaning: that giving is better than withholding for one who seeks closeness to Allah, glorified is He. ﴿And those are the successful﴾, meaning: those who attain what they seek, since they spent for the sake of Allah's Face in obedience to His command.

﴿And what you give in riba﴾. The majority read ātaytum with a long vowel (āytum), meaning "you gave." Mujāhid and Ḥumayd and Ibn Kathīr read it with a short vowel (ataytum), meaning "what you did." They all agree on the long-vowel reading in His saying: ﴿And what you give in zakāh﴾. The root meaning of ribā is increase. The short-vowel reading returns to the meaning of the long-vowel reading, because its meaning is "what you did in the manner of giving," just as you say: "I came in error" and "I came in rightness." The meaning in the verse is: what you give of excess that is free of any return. ﴿So that it may increase within the wealth of people﴾, meaning: so that it may grow and be purified within their wealth. ﴿It does not increase with Allah﴾, meaning: Allah does not bless it.

As-Suddī said: Ribā in this place is the gift that a man gives to his brother seeking a reward in return, for that does not increase with Allah, meaning its giver is not rewarded for it and there is no sin upon him. Qatādah and aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.

Al-Wāḥidī said: This is the view of the majority of the exegetes (mufassirūn).

Az-Zajjāj said: That is, a person gives something so that he may be repaid with more than it. That is not forbidden, but there is no reward for it, because the one who gives it seeks in return something greater than it.

Ash-Shaʿbī said: The meaning of the verse is that whatever a person serves another with, in order to benefit from him in his worldly life, that benefit which repays the service does not increase with Allah.

It has been said that this was forbidden to the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, based on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And do not confer favor seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:6]. Its meaning is: that you give and then take more than it in return.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning the gift given for reward (hibat al-thawāb).

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: And what is similar to it, of what a person does in order to be repaid for it.

ʿIkrimah said: Ribā is of two kinds: a lawful ribā and a forbidden ribā. As for the lawful ribā, it is the gift that a person gives seeking what is better than it, as in this verse.

It has also been said that what is in this verse is the forbidden ribā. According to this view, the meaning of "it does not increase with Allah" is that Allah does not reckon it as increase, but it belongs to the one from whom it was taken.

Al-Muhallab said: The scholars have differed concerning one who gives a gift seeking a reward. Mālik said: It is to be examined. If the one of its kind is one who seeks a reward from the recipient, then he has that right, like the gift of a poor man to a rich man, the gift of a servant to his master, and the gift of a man to his ruler. This is one of the two opinions of ash-Shāfiʿī. Abū Ḥanīfah said: He has no reward if he did not stipulate it. This is ash-Shāfiʿī's other opinion.

The majority read liyarbuwa with the letter yā' (third person), with the verb attributed to the pronoun referring to ribā. Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read it with tā' (second person) with a vowel on it, addressing the group, meaning: so that you may become people of increases.

Abū Mālik read: "li-tur'ūhā" [liturbūhā]. The meaning of the verse is that it does not grow with Allah, and He does not reward it, because He accepts only what is intended for His Face sincerely for Him alone. ﴿And what you give in zakāh, seeking the Face of Allah﴾, meaning: (p-1136) and what you give in charity without seeking a return by it, aiming only at what is with Allah. ﴿Those are the ones who multiply﴾. The muḍʿif (one who multiplies) is one who is multiplied beyond the manifold increases of good deeds, those who are given ten times its like up to seven hundredfold.

Al-Farrāʾ said: This is like their saying: muslim (one who has fat camels), mu ʿṭish (one who has thirsty camels), and muḍʿif (one who has weak camels), when he has camels that are fat, or thirsty, or weak.

Ubayy read al-muḍʿafūn with a fatḥah on the ʿayn, as a passive participle (ism mafʿūl).

﴿Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that?﴾ He, glorified is He, returned to arguing against the polytheists, and that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Causer of death and the Giver of life. Then He said, in the form of a question: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does any of that?﴾ It is known that they would say: there is none among them who does any of that, so the proof is established against them. Then He, glorified is He, declared Himself transcendent, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate﴾, meaning: they have glorified Him with a true glorification, and He is exalted above being subject to any of that. His saying ﴿of your partners﴾ is a predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam), with min indicating partial (lil-tabʿīḍ). The subject is the relative pronoun: that is, man yaf al (who does). ﴿Of that of yours﴾ is attached to something omitted, because it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of the thing mentioned after it. The min in min shayʾ is extra, for emphasis. He attributed the partners to them because they used to call them gods and assign to them a share of their wealth.

﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned.﴾ Glorified is He, explained that polytheism and sins are the cause of the appearance of corruption in the world.

Interpreters have differed concerning the meaning of the appearance of the corruption mentioned. It has been said: it is drought, the lack of vegetation, the decrease of provision, the prevalence of fear, and similar things. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: The corruption on land is the killing of the son of Adam his brother, meaning the killing of Qābīl of Hābīl. And at sea it is the king who used to seize every ship by force.

I wonder what proof led them to this distant specification and this strange determination, for the verse was revealed to Muḥammad (ﷺ), and the definite form of "corruption" indicates the category, so it includes every corruption occurring in the realms of land and sea.

As-Suddī said: The corruption is polytheism, which is the greatest corruption.

It may be said that although polytheism is the complete example among kinds of sins, there is no proof that it is specifically what is meant.

It has also been said: The corruption is the slump of prices and the scarcity of livelihood. It has been said: The corruption is the cutting of roads and oppression. It has been said: other than that, which is specification without proof.

The apparent meaning of the verse is the appearance of whatever it is correct to call corruption, whether it returns to the actions of the children of Adam, their sins, their committing of evil deeds, their severing of ties, their oppression, and their fighting one another, or returns to what comes from Allah, glorified is He, because of their sins, such as drought, prevalence of fear, death, decrease of crops, and decrease of fruits.

Al-barr (land) and al-baḥr (sea) are the well-known things. It has been said: al-barr is the deserts, and al-baḥr is the towns that are on water, as ʿIkrimah said, and the Arabs call great cities "seas." Mujāhid said: al-barr is what is of cities and villages not on a river, and al-baḥr is what is on the bank of a river. The first view is more preferable.

The meaning of al-barr would be the cities of the land, and the meaning of al-baḥr would be the cities of the sea, and what is connected to the cities of their farms and pastures. The bāʾ in ﴿by what﴾ indicates cause, and mā is either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah). ﴿So that He may make them taste part of what they have done﴾. The lām is connected to ẓahara (appeared), and it is the lām of cause, meaning: so that He may make them taste the punishment of part of their deeds, or the recompense of their deeds. ﴿Perhaps they will return﴾ from what they are engaged in of sins, and repent to Allah.

﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those before [you].﴾ When Allah, glorified is He, explained the appearance of corruption due to what the hands of the polytheists and the disobedient have earned, He explained to them the misguidance of those like them from people of earlier times, and commanded them to travel so that they might look at their traces and see how their end was. Their dwellings are empty and their lands are desolate and desolate like ʿĀd, Thamūd, and others of the groups of disbelievers. The clause ﴿most of them were polytheists﴾ is a new sentence explaining the condition in which they were, and clarifying the cause by which their end became what it became.

﴿So set your face toward the upright religion before there comes from Allah a Day which cannot be averted.﴾ This is an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his community who follow him in it. As if the meaning is: since corruption has appeared by the preceding cause, so set your face, O Muḥammad, etc.

Az-Zajjāj said: Make your direction the following of the upright religion, which is the straight Islam. ﴿Before there comes a Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Which cannot be averted﴾: no one is able to turn it back. Al-maradd is a verbal noun from radda. It has been said: The meaning is: clarify the truth and be thorough in establishing the proofs. ﴿From Allah﴾ is connected to ya'tī (comes), or to something omitted that is indicated by the verbal noun, meaning: no one turns it back from Allah. It has been said: The meaning could be that Allah does not turn it back, because of the connection of His eternal will to its coming, and in this there is weakness and bad manners toward Allah that are not hidden.

﴿On that Day they will be separated.﴾ The original form is yatafaṣṣaʿūn (they will split apart), and at-tafaṣṣuʿ is dispersal. It is said: "the people dispersed" (taṣaddaʿa al-qawm) when they scattered. From it is the saying of the poet:

"And we were like the two boon companions of Jadhīmah for a time of the age, until it was said: they will never separate."

What is meant by their dispersal here is that the people of Paradise will go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire will go to the Fire.

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, meaning: the recompense of his disbelief, which is the Fire. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare﴾, meaning: they prepare for themselves places in Paradise by righteous deeds. Al-mihād is the bed, and one says: "I spread the bed, spreading it out" when one lays it out and makes it ready. So He made the righteous deeds, which are the cause of entering Paradise, like building dwellings in Paradise and spreading their bedding.

It has been said: The meaning is: "upon themselves they are compassionate," from the saying about the compassionate one: a mother who spread and then lulled. The placing of the adverbial phrase in both places indicates restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ).

Mujāhid said: ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾ in the grave.

The lām in ﴿that He may reward those who believed﴾ is connected to yatafaṣṣaʿūn, or to yumahhidūn, meaning: they separate so that Allah may reward the believers with what they deserve of His bounty; or they prepare for themselves through righteous deeds so that He may reward them. It has been said: it is connected to something omitted.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: Its estimate is "that is so that He may reward," and the reference would be to what preceded in His saying: "whoever does" and "whoever disbelieves."

Abū Ḥayyān made the counterpart (qasīm) of His saying "those who believed and did righteous deeds" an omitted element, indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾, because it is a metonymy for His hatred of them, which requires His anger, glorified is He, and His anger entails His punishment.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 30, verse 38–46 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news﴾. That is: among the indications of the wondrous perfection of His power is the sending of winds as bearers of good news of rain, because they precede it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as a glad tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57]. The majority read "al-riyah" (the winds), while al-A'mash read "al-rih" (the wind) in the singular, intending the genus, on account of His saying ﴿bearers of good news﴾. The lam in His saying ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾ is connected to "yursil" (He sends), meaning: He sends the winds as bearers of good news, and He sends them that He may let you taste of His mercy, namely the rain and fertility. It was also said that it is connected to a deleted element, meaning: "and that He may let you taste, He sent them." It was also said that the waw is superfluous according to the view of those who permit that, so the lam is connected to "yursil." ﴿And that the ships may run by His command﴾ is coordinated with "li-yudhiqakum min rahmatihi" (that He may let you taste of His mercy), meaning: He sends the winds so that the ships may run upon the sea when they blow. When He attributed the running to the ships, He followed it with His saying "by His command." ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: that you may seek provision through the trade that the ships carry. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾ for these blessings, so that you single out Allah in worship and increase in obedience.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in riba﴾ (the verse), that he said: "Riba is of two kinds: riba that is no harm, and riba that is not permissible."
As for the riba that is no harm, it is a man's gift to another man, desiring its excess and multiples.

al-Bayhaqi related from him, who said: "This is the permissible riba: that one gives a gift desiring more than it, and there is neither reward nor sin for it. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade this specifically, saying: ﴿and do not give, seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 6]."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: ﴿And whatever you give in zakah﴾, he said: "It is the charity."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾, he said: "The land is the desert that has no river nearby, and the sea is what is of the cities and villages on the bank of a river."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding the verse, he said: "The decrease of blessing due to the deeds of the servants, so that they may repent."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also: ﴿so that they may return﴾, he said: "from sins."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: ﴿they will be divided﴾, he said: "they will disperse."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 30, verse 47–60 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples﴾ just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they brought them clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, they disbelieved. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, those who did the criminal acts, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾. This is an announcement from Allah, glorified is He, that His aid to His believing servants is binding upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not fail in His appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in the generosity toward His righteous servants. Some readers paused on "ḥaqqan" (truly) and made the subject of "kāna" a pronoun referring to it, with its predicate "ḥaqqan", meaning: and the retribution was true.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: This is weak. The correct view is that "naṣr al-mu'minīn" (the aid of the believers) is its subject, "ḥaqqan" is its predicate, and "ʿalaynā" is connected to "ḥaqqan", or to an omitted word which is an attribute of it.

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read "yursilu al-rīḥ" (in the singular). The rest read "al-riyāḥ" (in the plural). Abū ʿAmr said: whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a new, independent sentence, brought to explain the states of the winds previously mentioned; accordingly the sentence "And We certainly sent..." up to "And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers" is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it raises clouds﴾, that is, it agitates them from wherever they are, ﴿then He spreads them in the sky however He wills﴾, at one time moving, at another time stationary, at another time covering (the sky), at another time not covering, at another time over a great distance, and at another time over a short distance. The explanation of this verse has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Nur. ﴿And makes them fragments﴾ at another time, or after spreading them, makes them scattered pieces. "Kisaf" is the plural of "kisfah", and a "kisfah" is a piece of cloud.

Its explanation and the difference of recitation regarding it have already preceded. ﴿Then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾. "Al-wadq" is the rain, and "min khilālihi" means from its middle.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, that is, with the rain, ﴿whom He wills of His servants﴾, that is, their lands and their territories, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. "Idhā" here is the sudden (fujāʾiyyah) "idhā", meaning they suddenly became joyful at the arrival of the rain. "Istibshār" is joy.

﴿And even though, before it was sent down upon them﴾, that is, before the rain was sent down upon them, "in" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and in it is an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was that they, before it was sent down upon them... His saying "min qablihi" is a repetition for emphasis, as said by al-Akhfash and most grammarians, as transmitted from them by al-Naḥḥās.

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. The agent of giving life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He; and it is said: it refers to the effect (athar). This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained within the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. It has been disputed who these people given knowledge are: it is said: the angels; it is said: the prophets; it is said: the scholars of the nations; it is said: the believers of this Ummah. There is no objection to applying it to all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and decree. al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

It is also said: when the believers answered them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: "istakhaffa fulānun fulānan", meaning he considered him ignorant until he moved him to follow him in error.

The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed-by-dot... [sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: This is weak. The correct view is that "naṣr al-mu'minīn" (the aid of the believers) is its subject, "ḥaqqan" is its predicate, and "ʿalaynā" is connected to "ḥaqqan", or to an omitted word which is an attribute of it.

The explanation of this verse has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Nur. ﴿And makes them fragments﴾ at another time, or after spreading them, makes them scattered pieces. Its explanation and the difference of recitation regarding it have already preceded. ﴿Then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾. "Al-wadq" is the rain, and "min khilālihi" means from its middle.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, that is, with the rain, ﴿whom He wills of His servants﴾, that is, their lands and their territories, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. "Idhā" here is the sudden (fujāʾiyyah) "idhā", meaning they suddenly became joyful at the arrival of the rain. "Istibshār" is joy.

﴿And even though, before it was sent down upon them﴾, that is, before the rain was sent down upon them, "in" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and in it is an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was that they, before it was sent down upon them... His saying "min qablihi" is a repetition for emphasis, as said by al-Akhfash and most grammarians, as transmitted from them by al-Naḥḥās.

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. The agent of giving life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He; and it is said: it refers to the effect (athar). This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained within the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. It has been disputed who these people given knowledge are: it is said: the angels; it is said: the prophets; it is said: the scholars of the nations; it is said: the believers of this Ummah. There is no objection to applying it to all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and decree. al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes understood this as a matter of advancing and delaying, with the implied sense: "And those who were given knowledge said, in the Book of Allah..." The response of those given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in answer to their oath with an oath. Then they alerted them, by way of rebuke, that this "present" time in which they find themselves is ﴿the Day of Resurrection, but you used not to know﴾ that it is true; rather you used to hasten it, in denial and mockery.

It is also said: when the believers answered them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾, that is: in the like of that sealing, Allah seals the hearts of those who lack beneficial knowledge by which they would be guided to the truth and saved from falsehood.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, giving as the reason the truth of Allah's promise and that there is no failure in it, saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ over what you hear from them of harm and what you expect from them of disbelieving acts, for Allah has promised you victory over them, the exaltation of your proof, and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true, with no failure in it. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾, that is: let them not move you to levity or provoke you away from your religion and what you are upon, those who do not have certainty in Allah, do not believe His prophets, and do not believe in His books. The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: "istakhaffa fulānun fulānan", meaning he considered him ignorant until he moved him to follow him in error.

The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed-by-dot... [sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). The prohibition in the verse is of the type of: "lā arayannaka hāhunā" (I should not see you here).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim defends the honour of his brother except that it becomes a right upon Allah to keep the Fire of Hell away from him on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾. This report comes through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda'.

Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning His words ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾, that he said: "Pieces, some of them upon others." ﴿Then you see the rain﴾: he said, "The rain." ﴿coming out from its midst﴾: he said, "From between it."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ was revealed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling out to the people of Badr. The chain of this report is weak.

It is well known in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and elsewhere that Aisha used this verse to reject the report of some of the Companions that the Prophet (ﷺ) "called out to the people of the well of Badr." This is an instance of using a general text (al-'amm) to reject a particular report (al-khass). For the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when it was said to him, "You are calling out to decaying bodies": "You are no more able to hear what I say than they are." In Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, it is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) calling out to them, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are calling to them after three days? Can they hear? Allah says ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."

His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples﴾ just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they brought them clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, they disbelieved. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, those who did the criminal acts, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾. This is an announcement from Allah, glorified is He, that His aid to His believing servants is binding upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not fail in His appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in the generosity toward His righteous servants. "Kisaf" is the plural of "kisfah", and a "kisfah" is a piece of cloud.

﴿And even though, before it was sent down upon them﴾, that is, before the rain was sent down upon them, "in" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and in it is an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was that they, before it was sent down upon them... His saying "min qablihi" is a repetition for emphasis, as said by al-Akhfash and most grammarians, as transmitted from them by al-Naḥḥās.

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

[sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). Can they hear? Allah says ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. The agent of giving life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He; and it is said: it refers to the effect (athar). This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

It has been disputed who these people given knowledge are: it is said: the angels; it is said: the prophets; it is said: the scholars of the nations; it is said: the believers of this Ummah. There is no objection to applying it to all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and decree. al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes understood this as a matter of advancing and delaying, with the implied sense: "And those who were given knowledge said, in the Book of Allah..." The response of those given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in answer to their oath with an oath. It is also said: when the believers answered them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

It is said: "istaʿtabtuhu fa-aʿtabanī", meaning: I asked him to be pleased and he was pleased with me, and this is when you were an offender against him. The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, that is, every kind of example among the parables by which they are guided to the Oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and We have argued against them with every proof that demonstrates the falsehood of polytheism. ﴿And if you brought them a sign﴾ from the signs of the Qur'an that state this, or if you brought them a sign like the staff and the hand, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: You are not but falsifiers﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, and your companions, are not but falsifiers, people of falsehoods, following magic and what resembles it in falsehood.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, giving as the reason the truth of Allah's promise and that there is no failure in it, saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ over what you hear from them of harm and what you expect from them of disbelieving acts, for Allah has promised you victory over them, the exaltation of your proof, and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true, with no failure in it. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾, that is: let them not move you to levity or provoke you away from your religion and what you are upon, those who do not have certainty in Allah, do not believe His prophets, and do not believe in His books. The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: "istakhaffa fulānun fulānan", meaning he considered him ignorant until he moved him to follow him in error.

The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed-by-dot... [sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). The prohibition in the verse is of the type of: "lā arayannaka hāhunā" (I should not see you here).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim defends the honour of his brother except that it becomes a right upon Allah to keep the Fire of Hell away from him on the Day of Resurrection." Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning His words ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾, that he said: "Pieces, some of them upon others." ﴿Then you see the rain﴾: he said, "The rain." ﴿coming out from its midst﴾: he said, "From between it."

The chain of this report is weak.

It is well known in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and elsewhere that Aisha used this verse to reject the report of some of the Companions that the Prophet (ﷺ) "called out to the people of the well of Badr." This is an instance of using a general text (al-'amm) to reject a particular report (al-khass). For the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when it was said to him, "You are calling out to decaying bodies": "You are no more able to hear what I say than they are." In Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, it is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) calling out to them, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are calling to them after three days? Can they hear? Allah says ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."
