It is well known in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and elsewhere that Aisha used this verse to reject the report of some of the Companions that the Prophet (ﷺ) "called out to the people of the well of Badr." This is an instance of using a general text (al-'amm) to reject a particular report (al-khass). For the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when it was said to him, "You are calling out to decaying bodies": "You are no more able to hear what I say than they are." In Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, it is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) calling out to them, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are calling to them after three days? Can they hear? Allah says ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 30, verse 47–60 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples﴾ just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they brought them clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, they disbelieved. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, those who did the criminal acts, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾. This is an announcement from Allah, glorified is He, that His aid to His believing servants is binding upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not fail in His appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in the generosity toward His righteous servants. Some readers paused on "ḥaqqan" (truly) and made the subject of "kāna" a pronoun referring to it, with its predicate "ḥaqqan", meaning: and the retribution was true.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: This is weak. The correct view is that "naṣr al-mu'minīn" (the aid of the believers) is its subject, "ḥaqqan" is its predicate, and "ʿalaynā" is connected to "ḥaqqan", or to an omitted word which is an attribute of it.

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read "yursilu al-rīḥ" (in the singular). The rest read "al-riyāḥ" (in the plural). Abū ʿAmr said: whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a new, independent sentence, brought to explain the states of the winds previously mentioned; accordingly the sentence "And We certainly sent..." up to "And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers" is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it raises clouds﴾, that is, it agitates them from wherever they are, ﴿then He spreads them in the sky however He wills﴾, at one time moving, at another time stationary, at another time covering (the sky), at another time not covering, at another time over a great distance, and at another time over a short distance. The explanation of this verse has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Nur. ﴿And makes them fragments﴾ at another time, or after spreading them, makes them scattered pieces. "Kisaf" is the plural of "kisfah", and a "kisfah" is a piece of cloud.

Its explanation and the difference of recitation regarding it have already preceded. ﴿Then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾. "Al-wadq" is the rain, and "min khilālihi" means from its middle.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, that is, with the rain, ﴿whom He wills of His servants﴾, that is, their lands and their territories, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. "Idhā" here is the sudden (fujāʾiyyah) "idhā", meaning they suddenly became joyful at the arrival of the rain. "Istibshār" is joy.

﴿And even though, before it was sent down upon them﴾, that is, before the rain was sent down upon them, "in" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and in it is an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was that they, before it was sent down upon them... His saying "min qablihi" is a repetition for emphasis, as said by al-Akhfash and most grammarians, as transmitted from them by al-Naḥḥās.

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. The agent of giving life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He; and it is said: it refers to the effect (athar). This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained within the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. It has been disputed who these people given knowledge are: it is said: the angels; it is said: the prophets; it is said: the scholars of the nations; it is said: the believers of this Ummah. There is no objection to applying it to all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and decree. al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes understood this as a matter of advancing and delaying, with the implied sense: "And those who were given knowledge said, in the Book of Allah..." The response of those given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in answer to their oath with an oath. Then they alerted them, by way of rebuke, that this "present" time in which they find themselves is ﴿the Day of Resurrection, but you used not to know﴾ that it is true; rather you used to hasten it, in denial and mockery.

﴿So on that Day the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾, that is, their apology will not benefit them on that day, nor will their knowledge of the Resurrection profit them.

It is also said: when the believers answered them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

The majority read "lā tanfaʿu" with the feminine prefix. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with the masculine prefix. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It is said: "istaʿtabtuhu fa-aʿtabanī", meaning: I asked him to be pleased and he was pleased with me, and this is when you were an offender against him. The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, that is, every kind of example among the parables by which they are guided to the Oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and We have argued against them with every proof that demonstrates the falsehood of polytheism. ﴿And if you brought them a sign﴾ from the signs of the Qur'an that state this, or if you brought them a sign like the staff and the hand, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: You are not but falsifiers﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, and your companions, are not but falsifiers, people of falsehoods, following magic and what resembles it in falsehood.

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾, that is: in the like of that sealing, Allah seals the hearts of those who lack beneficial knowledge by which they would be guided to the truth and saved from falsehood.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, giving as the reason the truth of Allah's promise and that there is no failure in it, saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ over what you hear from them of harm and what you expect from them of disbelieving acts, for Allah has promised you victory over them, the exaltation of your proof, and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true, with no failure in it. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾, that is: let them not move you to levity or provoke you away from your religion and what you are upon, those who do not have certainty in Allah, do not believe His prophets, and do not believe in His books. The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: "istakhaffa fulānun fulānan", meaning he considered him ignorant until he moved him to follow him in error.

The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed-by-dot... [sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). The prohibition in the verse is of the type of: "lā arayannaka hāhunā" (I should not see you here).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim defends the honour of his brother except that it becomes a right upon Allah to keep the Fire of Hell away from him on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾. This report comes through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda'.

Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning His words ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾, that he said: "Pieces, some of them upon others." ﴿Then you see the rain﴾: he said, "The rain." ﴿coming out from its midst﴾: he said, "From between it."

The response of those given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in answer to their oath with an oath. Then they alerted them, by way of rebuke, that this "present" time in which they find themselves is ﴿the Day of Resurrection, but you used not to know﴾ that it is true; rather you used to hasten it, in denial and mockery.

﴿So on that Day the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾, that is, their apology will not benefit them on that day, nor will their knowledge of the Resurrection profit them.

It is also said: when the believers answered them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

The majority read "lā tanfaʿu" with the feminine prefix. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with the masculine prefix. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It is said: "istaʿtabtuhu fa-aʿtabanī", meaning: I asked him to be pleased and he was pleased with me, and this is when you were an offender against him. The literal sense of "aʿtabtuhu" is: I removed his displeasure. The meaning: they are not called upon to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called upon to do in the world.

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, that is, every kind of example among the parables by which they are guided to the Oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and We have argued against them with every proof that demonstrates the falsehood of polytheism. ﴿And if you brought them a sign﴾ from the signs of the Qur'an that state this, or if you brought them a sign like the staff and the hand, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: You are not but falsifiers﴾, that is: you, O Muhammad, and your companions, are not but falsifiers, people of falsehoods, following magic and what resembles it in falsehood.

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾, that is: in the like of that sealing, Allah seals the hearts of those who lack beneficial knowledge by which they would be guided to the truth and saved from falsehood.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, giving as the reason the truth of Allah's promise and that there is no failure in it, saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ over what you hear from them of harm and what you expect from them of disbelieving acts, for Allah has promised you victory over them, the exaltation of your proof, and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true, with no failure in it. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾, that is: let them not move you to levity or provoke you away from your religion and what you are upon, those who do not have certainty in Allah, do not believe His prophets, and do not believe in His books. The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: "istakhaffa fulānun fulānan", meaning he considered him ignorant until he moved him to follow him in error.

The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed-by-dot... [sic: with the letter khāʾ marked and fāʾ], and Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unmarked ḥāʾ and qāf from "istiḥqāq" (to deserve). The prohibition in the verse is of the type of: "lā arayannaka hāhunā" (I should not see you here).

Then he recited: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾. This report comes through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda'.

Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning His words ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾, that he said: "Pieces, some of them upon others." ﴿Then you see the rain﴾: he said, "The rain." ﴿coming out from its midst﴾: he said, "From between it."

The chain of this report is weak.

Can they hear? Allah says ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 30, verse 47–60 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples﴾ just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they brought them clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, they disbelieved. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who committed crime﴾, that is, those who did the criminal acts, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers﴾. This is an announcement from Allah, glorified is He, that His aid to His believing servants is binding upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not fail in His appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in the generosity toward His righteous servants. Some readers paused on "ḥaqqan" (truly) and made the subject of "kāna" a pronoun referring to it, with its predicate "ḥaqqan", meaning: and the retribution was true.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: This is weak. The correct view is that "naṣr al-mu'minīn" (the aid of the believers) is its subject, "ḥaqqan" is its predicate, and "ʿalaynā" is connected to "ḥaqqan", or to an omitted word which is an attribute of it.

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read "yursilu al-rīḥ" (in the singular). The rest read "al-riyāḥ" (in the plural). Abū ʿAmr said: whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a new, independent sentence, brought to explain the states of the winds previously mentioned; accordingly the sentence "And We certainly sent..." up to "And it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers" is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it raises clouds﴾, that is, it agitates them from wherever they are, ﴿then He spreads them in the sky however He wills﴾, at one time moving, at another time stationary, at another time covering (the sky), at another time not covering, at another time over a great distance, and at another time over a short distance. The explanation of this verse has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah and Surat al-Nur. ﴿And makes them fragments﴾ at another time, or after spreading them, makes them scattered pieces. "Kisaf" is the plural of "kisfah", and a "kisfah" is a piece of cloud.

Its explanation and the difference of recitation regarding it have already preceded. ﴿Then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾. "Al-wadq" is the rain, and "min khilālihi" means from its middle.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, that is, with the rain, ﴿whom He wills of His servants﴾, that is, their lands and their territories, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. "Idhā" here is the sudden (fujāʾiyyah) "idhā", meaning they suddenly became joyful at the arrival of the rain. "Istibshār" is joy.

﴿And even though, before it was sent down upon them﴾, that is, before the rain was sent down upon them, "in" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form, and in it is an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was that they, before it was sent down upon them... His saying "min qablihi" is a repetition for emphasis, as said by al-Akhfash and most grammarians, as transmitted from them by al-Naḥḥās.

Qaṭrub said: the pronoun in "qablihi" refers to the rain, meaning: and even though they were, before the sending down, before the rain.

It is also said: the meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and the rain. It is also said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, that is, before seeing it, and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.

It is also said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it is said: to the sending (irsāl), and it is said: to the rejoicing (istibshār).

The preponderant view is the first, and the rest of these views are all in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of "kāna" is ﴿despairing﴾, that is, hopeless or distressed. The verification of this matter has already preceded.

﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy﴾, arising from the sending down of rain, of plants, fruits and crops by which abundance and comfortable living come about. That is: look with the gaze of consideration and insight, so that you may infer from it the Oneness of Allah and His being singular in this wondrous making. The majority read "athari" (singular). Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read "āthār" (plural). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. The agent of giving life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He; and it is said: it refers to the effect (athar). This sentence is in the accusative position governed by "unẓur", that is: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.

al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywah read "tuḥyī" with the feminine prefix, its agent being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the effects according to the reading of those who read in the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ refers to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in affair, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, that is, of great and abundant power.

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. The pronoun in "faraʾūhu" returns to the crops and plants which were from the effect of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw it turned yellow from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after it had become green.

It is also said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.

It is also said: it refers to the effect implied by "al-āthār".

It is also said: it refers to the clouds, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more preferable.

The "lām" is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-mūṭṭi'ah), and the answer to the oath is ﴿they would certainly continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and this takes the place of the answer to the condition.

The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, which struck their crops with yellowness, they would certainly continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His favours. In this is evidence of the speed of their fluctuation, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, whereas this is not the state of the people of faith.

Then He likened them to the dead and to the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their failure to understand the realities and their lack of knowledge of what is right, ﴿nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their turning away from the truth, after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf of ears. The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Naml.

Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind from their error﴾, because they lack the benefit of sight as it should be, or because they lack insight. ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, that is: you make hear only these, because they are the people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from the effects to the Effector, ﴿so they are Muslims﴾, that is, submissive to the truth, following it.

﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness﴾. He, glorified is He, mentions another proof of the perfection of His power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "min ḍaʿf" is: from a drop (nuṭfah).

al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one possessing weakness.

It is also said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the body is consolidated until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, that is, at old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. The "shaybah" is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.

The majority read "ḍuʿf" with a ḍammah on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read it with a fatḥah. al-Jaḥdarī read with fatḥah in the first two and ḍammah in the third.

al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Jawharī said: "al-ḍaʿf" and "al-ḍuʿf" are the opposite of strength, and it is said: it is with fatḥah regarding opinion and with ḍammah regarding the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of His management, ﴿the Powerful﴾ to create what He intends. The Kufans permitted "min ḍaʿfin" with fatḥah on the ḍād and ʿayn.

﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, the Resurrection, and it was named "hour" because it arises in the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾, that is, they will swear that they remained in the world, or in their graves, for no more than an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay and this became fixed in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking their oath agreed with reality.

Ibn Qutaybah said: they lied at this time just as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure; and if they meant their stay in the graves, then they swore in ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh. ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: "afaka al-rajul" when he turns someone away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the like of that turning they used to be turned away.

It is said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth; and it is said: from good. The first is more preferable, and it is evidence that their oath was a lie.

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained within the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. It has been disputed who these people given knowledge are: it is said: the angels; it is said: the prophets; it is said: the scholars of the nations; it is said: the believers of this Ummah.
